public_rationale: The condition has not been established, so the forecast cannot be scored. The official UK report documents continuing consideration of reform, not the stipulated abandonment of creators' protections. That does not establish what happened in every other jurisdiction. The forecast also has no deadline, and no decisive event in the cited record settles its eventual outcome. Current original creation or increasing recycled content would not, by themselves, resolve it.
limitations: Unknown condition status is not a finding that no relevant law changed anywhere.
The wording leaves the qualifying legal change and the predicted quality decline materially ambiguous.
The evidence does not support either success or failure of the forecast.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: If copyright rules are rewritten for GenAI, eventually no one will create good new content and the internet will degrade into recycled AI output.
conditions: if lawmakers rewrite copyright rules for GenAI

statement.excerpt: But in the end, nobody will create good, fresh, new content anymore, and the internet will start eating its own tail. We will will all suffer in the end, fed a mediocre stew of regurgitate.
statement.document_title: The desperate race to save Generative AI

from_speaker: rewrite existing rules for the benefit of GenAI
abandoning principles that go back to the time of the printing press
nobody will create good, fresh, new content anymore
the internet will start eating its own tail
our_interpretation: The antecedent requires an enacted copyright change that materially weakens creators' control for the benefit of generative AI. A consultation, proposed law, or judicial application of existing law does not automatically qualify.
The plain reading predicts an eventual cessation of worthwhile original creation and an internet increasingly recycling prior material.
Good and mediocre are qualitative judgments; the wording supplies no agreed quality measure or recycled-content threshold.
In the end supplies no deadline. Continuing original creation at an intermediate date cannot alone refute this eventual forecast.
The wording does not identify which jurisdictions, changes, or scale of change would be sufficient to trigger the prediction.
criteria.support_condition: After a clearly qualifying legislative change, reliable evidence establishes the predicted enduring cessation of original creation and replacement by recycled material, with evidence connecting that outcome to the change.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After a clearly qualifying change, decisive evidence establishes that the predicted eventual cessation cannot occur. Continued creation over an arbitrarily chosen finite interval is insufficient because no deadline was supplied.

evidence.explanation: The surrounding section retains protection of human creativity as an objective and calls for further evidence on reform. This documents a policy process, not enactment of the sweeping change described in the forecast.
